notes: Reached via Claude-in-Chrome only (own tab), ES locale https://shop.mango.com/es/es/ (root geo-redirects to /gb/en; assigned country is Spain so the /es/es/ storefront was used throughout). robots.txt fetched same-origin (200): no ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai/Claude-Web/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot directive at all, so no Claude-specific disallow. TREE SOURCE: the Home department landing page https://shop.mango.com/es/es/h/home renders the complete Home mega-menu/SEO link block server-side. Enumerated every <a> pointing at /es/es/c/home/<slug>/<hash>: 79 distinct anchors covering the whole Home taxonomy at leaf granularity (e.g. SABANAS BAJERAS, FUNDAS ALMOHADAS, DIFUSORES SPRAY, JABONES, TOALLAS PLAYA). I then re-scanned the RAW outerHTML of the same page with a regex for /es/es/c/home/<slug>/<8-hex> to catch nodes present in the payload but not rendered as links: 74 unique slugs, all already in the visible nav, zero extra. FURNITURE SLUG SCAN over that union (mueble, silla, sillon, butaca, mesa, mesita, consola, sofa, cama, cabecero, escritorio, taburete, banco, banqueta, puf, estanteria, libreria, armario, comoda, aparador, vitrina, asiento, mecedora, reposapies, plus the English chair/table/desk/bed/stool/cabinet/shelving/sofa/bench/dresser): the ONLY hits were 'mantas-sofa' (sofa throws - textile), 'accesorios-mesa' and 'objetos-mesa' (table accessories / table objects - tableware), and 'set-the-table' (labelled COMEDOR = dining room, a curated Set-The-Table tableware rollup). No furniture node exists. SITEMAP GAP: https://shop.mango.com/sitemap.xml is refused by Akamai - 403 on a same-origin fetch and an Akamai 'Access Denied' page (Reference #18.91dc55b8...) on a real document navigation in the tab. Per the hard block rule I stopped requesting it and did NOT try variant sitemap paths. The mandatory sitemap cross-check was therefore replaced by (a) the raw-HTML slug scan above and (b) product-family scans described next. PRODUCT-LEVEL CROSS-CHECK: Mango product URLs are /es/es/p/home/<family-slug>/<product>/<id>, so the family slug of every rendered tile is a nav-independent view of the catalogue taxonomy. Checked the four nodes most likely to hide furniture: (1) Terrace https://shop.mango.com/es/es/c/home/terraza/d67318b7 - h1 'ACCESORIOS PARA LA TERRAZA' (Terrace accessories), totalItems=17, families present: cestas, velas-y-candelabros, maceteros; products are wicker/cotton baskets, terracotta planters, oak-footed glass lanterns, a decorative candle holder. No outdoor furniture anywhere on the site. (2) Kids Home https://shop.mango.com/es/es/c/home/kids-home/5dc32741 - h1 'KIDS HOME', totalItems=466, families: edredones-y-colchas-infantiles, fundas-nordicas-infantiles, fundas-almohada-infantiles, fundas-cojines-infantiles, ropa-cuna-y-minicuna, cestas-infantiles, peluches-y-juguetes, recien-nacido. Entirely kids bedding/textiles/soft toys/baskets - no cribs, kids beds, desks or changing tables. (3) Home decoration rollup https://shop.mango.com/es/es/c/home/decoracion/328fa15e - h1 'DECORACION PARA EL HOGAR', totalItems=718, families in the served batches: jarrones, alfombras, mantas-sofa, cortinas, fundas-cojines (vases + textiles). (4) Living-room accessories https://shop.mango.com/es/es/c/home/objetos-decoracion/009c9e08 - h1 'ACCESORIOS DE SALON', totalItems=51, families: objetos-decoracion, bandejas; every rendered product is a tray or a decorative object. CONCLUSION: Mango Home is a homeware line inside a fashion retailer - bedding and bath textiles, tableware/glassware, decorative objects, vases, mirrors, lamps, candles, homewear apparel and kids textiles. It sells no furniture of any kind in the Spanish storefront, so there is no furniture category to record. rows=[] is the correct answer, not a coverage failure. NOT USED / NOT NEEDED: no qty was taken because no furniture leaf exists. For reference the qty mechanism on this site is the pagination object embedded in the Next.js RSC payload of each category page ('totalItems'), which I confirmed varies per node (17 / 51 / 466 / 718) rather than being a site-wide constant. Site search was deliberately not used as a probe: robots.txt disallows the search paths, and per the brief a search-zero would not be proof of absence anyway.
